geo.terrain: largely mountainous with Great Caucasus Mountains in the north and Lesser Caucasus Mountains in the south; Kolkhet'is Dablobi (Kolkhida Lowland) opens to the Black Sea in the west; Mtkvari River Basin in the east; fertile soils in river valley flood plains and foothills of Kolkhida Lowland
geo.note: note 1: strategically located east of the Black Sea, Georgia controls much of the Caucasus Mountains and the routes through them ; ; note 2: the world's four deepest caves are all in Georgia, including two that are the only known caves on earth deeper than 2,000 m: Krubera Cave at -2,197 m (-7,208 ft; reached in 2012) and Veryovkina Cave at -2,212 (-7,257 ft; reached in 2018)

strategic.barriers: Greater Caucasus mountains to the north.
strategic.exposed: Russian-occupied Abkhazia and South Ossetia lie close to its east-west highway.
strategic.sea: Black Sea ports at Poti and Batumi; a corridor for Caspian oil and gas to Europe.
strategic.rivers: Kura flows into Azerbaijan.
strategic.note: A transit corridor between Russia, Turkey and the Caspian, Georgia faces strong Russian pressure.

res.list: timber, hydropower, manganese deposits, iron ore, copper, minor coal and oil deposits; coastal climate and soils allow for important tea and citrus growth

clim.hazards: earthquakes
clim.issues: air pollution, particularly in Rust'avi; heavy water pollution of Mtkvari River and the Black Sea; inadequate supplies of potable water; soil pollution from toxic chemicals; land and forest degradation; biodiversity loss; waste management
clim.climate: warm and pleasant; Mediterranean-like on Black Sea coast

lithium.processing: China refines most lithium chemicals, roughly two-thirds of global supply (IEA).
lithium.note: Essential for lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles and grid storage; mining is concentrated in Australia, Chile and China.

cobalt.processing: China is the leading refiner, producing roughly three-quarters of refined cobalt.
cobalt.note: Used in battery cathodes and jet-engine superalloys. DR Congo supplies about three-quarters of mined cobalt and imposed export quotas in late 2025.

rare_earths.processing: China separates and refines about 90% of rare earths and makes most permanent magnets.
rare_earths.note: Needed for magnets in motors, wind turbines and missiles. China tightened export controls in 2025, showing its leverage.

graphite.processing: China produces over 90% of battery-grade graphite anode material, natural and synthetic.
graphite.note: The largest mineral component of lithium-ion battery anodes; China dominates both mining (about 78%) and processing.

nickel.processing: Indonesia and China dominate refining, much of it in Chinese-owned smelters in Indonesia.
nickel.note: Used in stainless steel and high-energy batteries. Indonesia's ore export ban drew processing onshore and now gives it about two-thirds of mined supply.

copper.processing: China produces nearly half of world refined copper (about 14 of 29 million tonnes in 2025, USGS).
copper.note: The backbone of electrical grids, motors and electronics; demand rises with electrification and data centres.

gallium.processing: China produces about 99% of primary gallium, recovered as a by-product of alumina refining.
gallium.note: Vital for chips such as gallium nitride radar and power electronics. China has restricted gallium exports since 2023.

uranium.processing: Enrichment is concentrated in Russia, Europe (Urenco, Orano) and China; Russia holds the largest share of capacity.
uranium.note: Fuels nuclear power; Kazakhstan alone mines about two-fifths. Western utilities are cutting reliance on Russian enrichment.

manganese.processing: China refines over 90% of high-purity manganese used in batteries and most electrolytic manganese metal.
manganese.note: Essential to steelmaking with no good substitute; also used in battery cathodes. South Africa holds about 70% of world resources.

platinum.processing: Most platinum-group metals are refined where mined, chiefly in South Africa and Russia (Norilsk, which leads palladium).
platinum.note: Used in catalytic converters, hydrogen electrolysers and fuel cells. South Africa's Bushveld Complex holds most world reserves.
